name: Pfaffenhofen
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Oberinntal with one of Tirol’s oldest continuously inhabited castles and the ruins of Burg Hörtenberg.
beschreibung:
Overview

Pfaffenhofen is situated in the Tyrolean Upper Inn Valley in the district of Innsbruck-Land at an elevation of 642 metres, located on the southern riverbank directly opposite the market town of Telfs. This historic residential municipality is home to approximately 1,480 inhabitants and covers seven square kilometres, stretching from the green banks of the Inn across sunny hillside terraces up into the Northern Stubai Alps, culminating at Mount Hocheder at 2,798 metres. While Telfs across the river serves as the bustling commercial centre, Pfaffenhofen has carefully preserved its peaceful rural atmosphere, village charm, and profound heritage. The two towns are seamlessly connected via road bridges and a shared railway station. Geographically, Pfaffenhofen delights residents and guests with sweeping vistas of the towering south walls of Hohe Munde, sunny low-mountain plateaus, and forested ridges.

History

Settlement in the area dates back to the Iron Age, evidenced by a prehistoric Rhaetian hilltop settlement of the Fritzens-Sanzeno culture discovered beneath the castle ruins. Remarkable excavations beneath the parish church uncovered sacred 5th-century foundations with a bishop's bench (synthronon), supporting the thesis that Pfaffenhofen served as an early Christian itinerant bishopric. The village was first documented in 1197 as Phafenhofen. High above the village looms Hörtenberg Castle, documented in 1239 as the seat of the Counts of Eschenlohe and acquired in 1286 by Count Meinhard II of Tyrol, serving for centuries as the judicial centre of the Hörtenberg court. In 1706, a catastrophic lightning strike detonated the gunpowder magazine, blowing up much of the fortress; its imposing five-storey keep remains intact. The late Gothic Parish Church of the Assumption preserves a subterranean crypt displaying early Christian excavations and Roman stones. In the village square, the Narrenbrunnen fountain celebrates deep-rooted carnival heritage.

Getting There

Pfaffenhofen boasts prime transport connections across the central Inn Valley. By automobile, drivers access the village via the Inntal Autobahn A12 using exits Telfs-West or Telfs-Ost, crossing the Inn River via federal road B171 in around 25 minutes from Innsbruck. Rail travellers benefit directly from the Telfs-Pfaffenhofen railway station on the Arlberg Railway line, situated right within Pfaffenhofen municipal territory. The station is served every half hour by Tyrolean S-Bahn lines S4 and S5 as well as Regional-Express (REX) trains, offering swift transfers to Innsbruck. From the station and village square, VVT regional buses connect locally to Telfs, Rietz, and Mieming. Cyclists can pedal along the scenic Inn Valley Cycle Path R3 on the quiet southern riverbank.

Tips

A favourite local excursion is the hike up to Hörtenberg Castle ruins at approximately 800 metres above sea level: a signposted forest trail leads up from the village square in roughly 45 minutes to the preserved keep, which commands a breathtaking panorama across Telfs, the Inn Valley, and the Hohe Munde. During summer, the atmospheric open-air castle courtyard hosts open-air theatre performances. Cultural visitors should explore the archaeological crypt beneath the Parish Church of the Assumption. For hikers and mountain bikers, the Pfaffenhofener Alm at 1,694 metres in the Stubai Alps offers authentic Tyrolean alpine hospitality. Seasoned mountaineers can continue from the alpine pasture up Sonnkarköpfl (2,262 m) to the panoramic summit of Mount Hocheder (2,798 m).
